The internal-angle sum of a pentagon is \(540^\circ\), so  
\[
\angle C=540^\circ-(90^\circ+90^\circ+45^\circ+45^\circ)=270^\circ.
\]

Place \(AE\) on the \(x\)-axis with  
\[
A=(0,0),\qquad E=(20,0).
\]
Since \(\angle A=\angle E=90^\circ\) and \(B,C,D\) are on the same side of \(AE\), the sides \(AB\) and \(DE\) are vertical. Let  
\[
AB=b,\qquad B=(0,b).
\]
At \(B\), \(\angle B=45^\circ\), so \(BC\) runs downward at a \(45^\circ\) angle. Since \(BC=14\sqrt2\),
\[
C=(14,b-14).
\]
For \(C\) to lie above \(AE\), we need \(b>14\).

At \(D\), \(\angle D=45^\circ\), so \(DC\) is obtained from the downward ray \(DE\) by turning \(45^\circ\). Write \(CD=x\sqrt2\). Then the horizontal displacement from \(C\) to \(D\) is \(x\). But the total horizontal displacement from \(B\) (at \(x=0\)) to \(D\) (at \(x=20\)) is \(20\), so
\[
14+x=20\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=6.
\]
Hence \(CD=6\sqrt2\). The vertical drop from \(B\) to \(D\) is \(14-6=8\), so
\[
DE=b-8.
\]

The pentagon can be viewed as trapezoid \(ABDE\) minus right triangle \(BCD\).  
Trapezoid \(ABDE\) has area
\[
\frac{AB+DE}{2}\cdot AE=\frac{b+(b-8)}{2}\cdot20=20b-80.
\]
Triangle \(BCD\) has legs \(BC=14\sqrt2\) and \(CD=6\sqrt2\) meeting at a right angle, so
\[
[BCD]=\frac12(14\sqrt2)(6\sqrt2)=84.
\]
Thus the pentagon’s area is
\[
K=(20b-80)-84=20b-164.
\]

We need \(16\mid K\):
\[
20b-164\equiv0\pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow 4b+12\equiv0\pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow 4b\equiv4\pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow b\equiv1\pmod4.
\]

Also \(b\) is an integer with
\[
14<b<2026.
\]
The admissible values are
\[
17,21,25,\dots,2025.
\]
The number of terms is
\[
\frac{2025-17}{4}+1=502+1=503.
\]

\[
\boxed{503}
\]
